translationRepairs: 列傳第十九 is the chapter serial, not a reign year; 'Biographies 19' matches the Chinese.
Xie Lingyun, Commander of the Left Guard to the Heir Apparent, killed men more than once; Imperial Censor Xu Zhunzhi was removed for failing to impeach him.
Xie Lingyun, Commander of the Left Guard to the Heir Apparent, killed men on his own authority; Imperial Censor Wang Zhunzhi was removed for failing to impeach him.
The censor is 王准之 (Wang, not Xu). 輒殺人 means killing on his own authority, not specifically 'more than once'.
Tan was already dead; his son Ling Sun, Grand Administrator of Shanyang, surrendered himself to the Minister of Justice.
Tan was already dead; his son Lingsun, Grand Administrator of Shanyang, surrendered himself to the Minister of Justice.
令孫 is one given name and should be romanized Lingsun, not two English words.

An edict ordered external deliberation. Yigong had Secretariat Director Liu Yuanjing accuse Xingzong and Director Yuan Min of privately promising each other appointments, selecting each other, disordering government, and befouling great policy.

An edict ordered external deliberation. Yigong had Secretariat Director Liu Yuanjing accuse Xingzong and Director Yuan Minsun of privately promising each other appointments, selecting each other, disordering government, and befouling great policy.
袁湣孫 is the three-character name Yuan Minsun; dropping 孫 as Yuan Min is a naming error.

An edict ordered external detailed deliberation; Yigong had Secretariat Director Liu Yuanjing memorialize that Xingzong and Director Yuan Min had privately promised each other appointments, selecting each other and disordering the group, harming government and befouling great policy.

An edict ordered external detailed deliberation; Yigong had Secretariat Director Liu Yuanjing memorialize that Xingzong and Director Yuan Minsun had privately promised each other appointments, selecting each other and disordering the group, harming government and befouling great policy.
The literal field likewise shortens 袁湣孫 to Yuan Min; restoring Yuan Minsun is required.

Before long Faxing was killed, Shangzhi imprisoned, Yigong and Shibo executed; Xingzong was restored as Senior Administrator to Prince Ziye of Linhai's Forward Army and Grand Administrator of Nan Command, acting Governor of Jing—he did not go.

Before long Faxing was killed, Shangzhi imprisoned, Yigong and Shibo executed; Xingzong was restored as Senior Administrator to Prince Zixu of Linhai's Forward Army and Grand Administrator of Nan Command, acting Governor of Jing—he did not go.
子頊 is Zixu; Ziye would be a different given name (子業).

Before long Faxing was killed, Shangzhi imprisoned, Yigong and Shibo all executed; Xingzong was restored as Senior Administrator to Prince Ziye of Linhai's Forward Army and Grand Administrator of Nan Command, acting as Governor of Jing Province—he did not go.

Before long Faxing was killed, Shangzhi imprisoned, Yigong and Shibo all executed; Xingzong was restored as Senior Administrator to Prince Zixu of Linhai's Forward Army and Grand Administrator of Nan Command, acting as Governor of Jing Province—he did not go.
The literal field repeats Ziye for 子頊; Zixu is the correct romanization.

At each court feast the Emperor beat the hundred ministers with a club; from General of Agile Cavalry Prince Jian'an Xiuren downward, Palace Attendant Yuan Min and the rest all suffered abuse and dragging—only Xingzong was spared.

At each court feast the Emperor beat the hundred ministers with a club; from General of Agile Cavalry Prince Jian'an Xiuren downward, Palace Attendant Yuan Minsun and the rest all suffered abuse and dragging—only Xingzong was spared.
侍中袁湣孫 is Yuan Minsun; the English must retain 孫.
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon also headed the Court of the Imperial Clan.
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon also headed the Court of the Palace Guards.
衛尉 is the palace-guard chamberlain, not 宗正 (Imperial Clan).
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon also headed the Court of the Imperial Clan.
He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon also concurrently headed the Court of the Palace Guards (Weiwei).
衛尉 is not the Imperial Clan, but 'headed the Guard Commandant' is ungrammatical; 尋領 means he concurrently headed that office.
When Zheqi was pacified, Yuan Yan's head arrived in a box; an edict ordered Xingzong to ascend the South Yeb Gate tower to view it.
When Zheqi was pacified, Yuan Yan's head arrived in a box; an edict ordered Xingzong to ascend the South Lateral Gate tower to view it.
南掖門 is the South Lateral Gate; 'Yeb' is not a valid reading of 掖.

When the affair was settled, Xingzong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shichang; he declined and was refused; it was changed to Marquis of Le'an; state salary and clerical labor he ultimately did not accept.

When the affair was settled, Xingzong was enfeoffed as Earl of Shichang County; he declined and was refused; it was changed to Earl of Le'an County; state salary and clerical labor he ultimately did not accept.
始昌縣伯 and 樂安縣伯 are county earldoms (伯), not marquisates (侯).
The Secretariat drafted an edict to persuade Yan; Xingzong said: "The realm is settled; this is the day Yan would submit. Your Majesty should bestow a handwritten edition of several lines.
The Secretariat drafted an edict to persuade Yan; Xingzong said: "The realm is settled; this is the day Yan would submit. Your Majesty should bestow a handwritten edict of several lines.
手詔 is a handwritten edict, not an edition.
Zhensun's grandson Jingxian was very talented; Xingzong kept company with him.
Zhensun's son Jingxian was very talented; Xingzong kept company with him.
珍孫子景先 is Jingxian, son of Zhensun; 子 here is kinship 'son', not part of a 'grandson' reading.
When Jingxian was Grand Administrator of Poyang, Prince Jin'an Ziluan rebelled; he transferred to Jingling and was killed by Wu Xi.
When Jingxian was Grand Administrator of Poyang, Prince Jin'an Zixun rebelled; he transferred to Jingling and was killed by Wu Xi.
晉安王子勳 is Prince Zixun; Ziluan is a different prince's name.
Commander of the Left Guard to the Heir Apparent Wang Xi's wife Fan was an intelligent woman with talent and learning.
Fan, wife of Wang Xi, Commander of the Left Guard to the Heir Apparent, was an intelligent woman with talent and learning.
太子左率 modifies 王錫, not an heir apparent named Wang Xi; reordering removes a real misparse.
His wife Lady Liu died early; one daughter was very young; his nephew Yuan Yan had just borne a son Tuan when his wife Lady Liu also died; Xingzong's elder sister was Yan's mother.
His wife Lady Liu died early; one daughter was very young; his nephew Yuan Yan had just had a son Tuan when Yan's wife Lady Liu also died; Xingzong's elder sister was Yan's mother.
始生子 cannot take 'borne' of the male nephew, and the second 妻劉氏 is Yan's wife.
Earlier when Zun was at Linhai, commoner Yang Yuansun posted maid Cailan with fellow villager Huang Quan; they agreed she would bear a child and pay nursing wages.
Earlier when Zun was at Linhai, commoner Yang Yuansun pledged the maid Cailan to fellow villager Huang Quan; they agreed she would bear a child and that nursing wages would be paid.
貼與 is a pledge or pawn of the maid to Huang Quan, not 'posting' her.

He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier beneath the fragrant orange: "You truly do not understand affairs."

He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier beneath the fragrant stool: "You truly do not understand affairs."
香橙 is a fragrant stool (橙 for 凳), not the fruit orange.

He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier to the ground beneath the fragrant orange and said: "You truly do not understand affairs."

He once memorialized to appoint Langya Wang Yun as Attendant Within the Gates; the Emperor disliked his not taking part in joint administration and pushed the white dossier to the ground beneath the fragrant stool and said: "You truly do not understand affairs."
The literal field likewise misreads 香橙 as orange fruit rather than a stool.
He held the dossier straight out and left, ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialized in protest to resign.
He held the dossier straight out and left, ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialize in protest to resign.
'wished to memorialized' is ungrammatical; the infinitive memorialize is required.
He thereupon held the dossier straight out and left, immediately ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialized in protest to resign.
He thereupon held the dossier straight out and left, immediately ordered his carriage and departed, and still wished to memorialize in protest to resign.
The literal field has the same ungrammatical 'to memorialized'.
